script: A 2,000-year-old Xiongnu tomb in Mongolia held a Roman glass cup and Han-style jade discs
Its nine stone layers stretch 240 feet—larger than the Great Sphinx
Jade 'bi' discs show Han influence, but with unique, irregular designs
A quartz-inlaid silver horse ornament and wooden carriage hint at elite status
The tomb's size and artifacts reveal deep Eurasian trade links from China to Rome
DNA analysis of coffin remains may identify the occupant and their lineage
Did the Xiongnu blend Han and Roman customs to signal power and status?
Tap the link below for the full case file.
short.description:
A 2,000-year-old Xiongnu tomb in Mongolia contained a Roman glass cup and Han-inspired jade decorations. The tomb, part of a large burial complex, shows trade links between Central Asia, China, and the Roman Empire. The jade discs are irregular and engraved, suggesting adaptation of Han burial customs. The Roman glass cup’s origin is uncertain and requires further testing. Source: Live Science, https://www.livescience.com/archaeology/2-000-year-old-tomb-of-an-elite-nomad-in-mongolia-contained-a-roman-glass-cup-and-han-dynasty-inspired-jade-decorations
Full case file: https://youtu.be/BDB2DcM3w14
